newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian state firms to participate in Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian state firms to participate in Busang.

text.p: Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Tuesday Indonesian state-owned companies would have the opportunity to participate in the Busang gold development at the production level.
Speaking at a Jakarta news conference, Sudjana did not specify the state-owned companies.
However, tin miner PT Tambang Timah and nickel and gold miner PT Aneka Tambang have both indicated their interest in participating in Busang.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd announced on Monday a joint venture agreement under which the company would have 45 percent of the richest part of the Busang find, its Indonesian partners and their partners would get 30 percent, the government 10 percent and U.S. company Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc 15 percent.
Freeport is to develop and operate the mine.
Sudjana said the state-owned companies `will be given the chance to participate at the production stage to reduce their risk`.
A senior official of the Mines and Energy Ministry also told the news conference the Finance Ministry would hold the government's 10 percent stake.
A senior official of the Mines and Energy Ministry also said the Indonesian government will soon approve 68 outstanding contracts of work (COWS) for the mining industry.
